findings.reason: a worker building the stated fixture gets a duty that never enters the measured branch, and must invent an armed follower, a superseded stored review and a scoring classification the plan does not mention; the plan's claim that its fixture "reaches the measured path" is false as written.
findings.text: the fixture clause ("each delivered run has at least one stored review record … and each duty is aged past `_reflex_review_window_seconds()`") still does not reach `_open_review_refusal`'s `run_ids` call: `_reflex_open_refusal` is reached only at reckon/crew/obligations.py:1974, inside `if item["kind"] == "review-missing" and classification == "scoring"` (:1955) and only when `_reflex_owns_review(project, pointer)` is true (:1966, which needs `runs.follower_state(...)["live"]` for the pointer's session, :726-736); the duty reads `review-missing` only when the stored review is open and covers a *superseded* head (:1920-1954), its newest review carries no undisposed blocking finding (:1858-1892), no refusal record speaks for the revision (:1911), and no queued review placement exists (:1943-1952) — a stored review for the current head turns the duty into `review-ready` and never calls `run_ids`, so the test's own positive assertion (that `_open_review_refusal` reached the call for every run) cannot pass on the fixture the plan states

findings.reason: the measure must distinguish the two offered fixes and must not attribute the index build to the duty, otherwise the worker either reports a false failure or hoists the read into a shape the section did not intend.
findings.text: the gate "one obligations pass calls `_load_aggregate` at most once per project, counted through a patch" cannot hold at head on the fresh temporary crew home the fixture specifies: `ledger.read_records` calls `_load_aggregate` when its SQLite index stamp is cold (reckon/ledger.py:1535, `aggregate_changed = meta.get("stamp") != aggregate_stamp`), which is exactly the first pass over a newly built temp home, so the count is (index build) + (duty reads); and because the patch counts entries to `_load_aggregate`, the second offered fix — serving `run_ids` from a stat-validated cache placed inside `_load_aggregate`/`_store._load_json_envelope` — keeps the count at the number of duties, so a correct implementation of an offered branch fails the gate

findings.reason: the section already instructs the worker to measure "whether `_load_aggregate` is served from a cache" and to add one if not, so the inaccurate premise costs the worker one verification and changes no deliverable; naming the memo's home would only sharpen the brief.
findings.text: "`run_ids` is served from the stat-validated cache the ledger already keeps" overstates what exists: the aggregate read is `_store._load_json_envelope` (reckon/_store.py:422-447), an unconditional `path.read_text()` + `json.loads` per call, and the ledger's only stat-validated cache is the per-run document memo `read_document` (`_RUN_DOCUMENT_KIND`, reckon/ledger.py:1283-1298) — and the natural home for an aggregate memo, `reckon/_store.py`, is outside the section's write paths

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `ledger.run_ids` (reckon/ledger.py:1051), `_load_aggregate` (reckon/ledger.py:992), `_open_review_refusal` (reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2474, the `run_ids` call at :2516 exactly), `_reflex_open_refusal` (reckon/crew/obligations.py:779) and `_reflex_review_window_seconds` (:739) all resolve, and `docs/plans/a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking.html` exists.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the gate counts `_load_aggregate` calls per project to prove the fix, but `ledger.read_records` also calls `_load_aggregate` (reckon/ledger.py:1535) when its index stamp is cold, which a fresh temporary crew home is, so the bound "at most once per project" is not reachable from the fixture with either offered fix applied.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the test log and the live per-tick before/after figures are declared under the run directory, which is durable on the shared config home, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `tests/test_a_review_duty_reads_the_ledger_once_per_pass.py` names the mechanism and carries no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section's own mechanism claim that the offered cache is "the stat-validated cache the ledger already keeps" describes a cache that exists for per-run documents only (`ledger.read_document`, `_RUN_DOCUMENT_KIND`, reckon/ledger.py:1293), not for the aggregate `run_ids` reads; the aggregate read in `_load_json_envelope` is uncached (`reckon/_store.py:422-447`, a plain `read_text` + `json.loads` every call).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable (the ledger read hoisted or cached once per pass), and the "or" is two implementations of that one change, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15 declares no depends-on, informs or gates edge (`data-links=""`), and it consumes nothing another section must land first; the ledger, obligations and review-dispatch modules it names all exist at the reviewed revision.
